retrieved_items.title: Activate drought anticipatory action coordination
retrieved_items.rationale: Severe rainfall deficit and high exposure require immediate coordination before impacts worsen.
actions: Activate a district drought coordination meeting with agriculture, water, livestock, health and disaster risk management offices.
Verify water-point status, pasture condition and livestock movement using local officers and community reports.
Prioritize high-exposure kebeles, wards or settlements for early action support.
Prepare early warning messages explaining expected impacts and recommended household-level preparedness actions.
Review contingency resources for water trucking, livestock feed support, veterinary outreach and targeted cash or voucher support.
retrieved_items.source_note: Prototype local knowledge item for drought trigger-level early action planning.

retrieved_items.title: Provide drought advisory to farmers and pastoralists
retrieved_items.rationale: Farmers and pastoralists need practical guidance on water, pasture, crops and livestock management.
actions: Advise communities to conserve water and protect remaining water sources.
Promote early livestock feed planning, fodder conservation and strategic herd movement where appropriate.
Monitor crop wilting, pasture degradation and livestock body condition during field visits.
Share drought-tolerant crop, forage and animal health messages through extension channels.
Report worsening field conditions to district coordination structures.
retrieved_items.source_note: Prototype local knowledge item for agriculture and livestock extension response.

retrieved_items.title: Prepare anticipatory drought support package
retrieved_items.rationale: Trigger-level drought risk requires rapid planning for targeted support before losses escalate.
actions: Review beneficiary targeting using exposure, vulnerability and community ground-truth reports.
Coordinate with local government to avoid duplication of early action support.
Pre-position or plan support for water access, livestock feed, animal health and household preparedness.
Use community reports to verify where field stress is already emerging.
Prepare monitoring indicators to track whether early actions are reducing impacts.
retrieved_items.source_title: Forecast2Action NGO drought early action guide
retrieved_items.source_note: Prototype local knowledge item for NGO anticipatory action planning.

retrieved_items.title: Increase drought preparedness and monitoring
retrieved_items.rationale: Warning-level drought risk requires intensified monitoring and early preparedness before conditions become critical.
actions: Increase monitoring of rainfall performance, water points, pasture condition and crop stress.
Brief local officers and community focal persons about the current warning level.
Prepare drought advisory messages for farmers, pastoralists and vulnerable households.
Collect community observations to confirm whether impacts are already emerging.
Review preparedness options for water, feed, veterinary and social protection support.
retrieved_items.source_note: Prototype local knowledge item for drought warning-level preparedness.

retrieved_items.title: Activate flood preparedness and public safety actions
retrieved_items.rationale: Trigger-level heavy rainfall risk requires immediate preparedness and public safety messaging.
actions: Activate local flood preparedness coordination.
Issue clear public safety messages for flood-prone areas.
Prioritize monitoring of river crossings, low-lying settlements and roads.
Prepare evacuation support for highly exposed communities where needed.
Use community reports to identify flooded roads, river overflow and blocked drainage.
retrieved_items.source_title: Forecast2Action flood trigger early action guide
retrieved_items.source_note: Prototype local knowledge item for trigger-level heavy rainfall and flood preparedness.
